conbody.p: This section describes the mandatory and recommended configuration settings for Impala. They depend on whether the Impala daemons run on the same hosts as the storage, that is, the HDFS DataNodes or the Ozone Datanodes. If Impala is installed using cluster management software, some of these configurations might be completed automatically. If you want to customize your environment, consider making the changes described in this topic.

p.b: If Impala runs on the same hosts as the storage:

ul.li: You must enable short-circuit reads, whether or not Impala was installed with cluster management software. This setting goes in the Impala configuration settings, not the Hadoop-wide settings. See Mandatory: Short-Circuit Reads.
Keep block location tracking turned on, so that Impala reads the data locally. It is on by default and needs no configuration. See Block Location Tracking.

conbody.p: If Impala does not run on the same hosts as the storage, for example when Impala runs in containers:

ul.li: We recommend turning off block location loading, which makes loading and refreshing tables much faster. See Turning Off Block Location Loading.
Short-circuit reads do not apply, because Impala never reads the data from the local host.
To reduce the cost of remote reads, enable the data cache. See .

conbody.p: In both cases, you can optionally enable native checksumming for optimal performance. See Optional: Native Checksumming.

section.title: Mandatory: Short-Circuit Reads
section.p: Enabling short-circuit reads allows Impala to read local data directly from the file system. This removes the need to communicate through the DataNodes, improving performance. This setting also minimizes the number of additional copies of data. Short-circuit reads requires libhadoop.so (the Hadoop Native Library) to be accessible to both the server and the client. libhadoop.so is not available if you have installed from a tarball. You must install from an .rpm, .deb, or parcel to use short-circuit local reads.

p.b: To configure DataNodes for short-circuit reads:

ol.li: Copy the client core-site.xml and hdfs-site.xml configuration files from the Hadoop configuration directory to the Impala configuration directory. The default Impala configuration location is /etc/impala/conf.

dfs.client.read.shortcircuit dfs.domain.socket.path On all Impala nodes, configure the following properties in
Impala's copy of hdfs-site.xml as shown: <property> <name>dfs.client.read.shortcircuit</name> <value>true</value> </property>
<property> <name>dfs.domain.socket.path</name> <value>/var/run/hdfs-sockets/dn</value> </property>

li.p: If /var/run/hadoop-hdfs/ is group-writable, make sure its group is root.

ol.li: After applying these changes, restart all DataNodes.

section.title: Block Location Tracking
section.p: For files on HDFS, Ozone, and Alluxio, Impala loads the block locations of each file, that is, which hosts and disks store each block. The scheduler uses them to assign each scan range to an Impala daemon running on a host that stores a replica, so the data is read locally, for example with short-circuit reads, and the I/O is spread across the disks of the host. Block locations are loaded by default and need no configuration.

Data locality only matters when the Impala daemons run on the same hosts as the HDFS DataNodes or Ozone Datanodes. If they do not, we recommend turning off block location loading, as described in Turning Off Block Location Loading. It makes loading and refreshing tables much faster, and the table metadata takes less memory.

section.title: Turning Off Block Location Loading
section.p: In and higher, you can turn off block location loading through the Hadoop configuration. We recommend doing this when Impala does not run on the same hosts as HDFS or Ozone, for example when Impala runs in containers. In that case the block locations bring no benefit, but catalogd still fetches them for every file when it loads or refreshes a table, which is expensive for tables with many files.

Set the following properties in the core-site.xml file in the Impala configuration directory. They are Hadoop configuration properties, not startup flags, so they do not appear in the --help output or on the /varz page; the /hadoop-varz page of the impalad and catalogd web UI shows the values in effect.

ul.li: impala.preload-block-locations-for-scheduling.scheme.scheme: applies to the filesystems with the given URI scheme, such as hdfs or ofs.

impala.preload-block-locations-for-scheduling.authority.authority: applies to the filesystems with the given URI authority, such as mycluster for hdfs://mycluster/... or nn-host:8020 for hdfs://nn-host:8020/.... Use it when several storage clusters share the same scheme.

section.p: All of them default to true. Setting any of them to false turns off block location loading for the matching filesystems, and a true value at another level cannot turn it back on. For example, if the hdfs scheme is set to false and the mycluster authority to true, Impala does not load block locations for hdfs://mycluster/. Any value other than true counts as false.
Only the hdfs, ofs, o3fs, and alluxio schemes have block locations, so the properties only affect those. Impala never loads block locations for other filesystems, such as S3, ADLS, ABFS, or GCS.

Each daemon reads these properties once at startup, so restart catalogd and the impalad daemons after changing them.
section.note: Use the same settings on catalogd and on every coordinator. If catalogd does not load block locations but a coordinator expects them, the coordinator skips the files that have no blocks, and queries silently return too few rows. If catalogd loads block locations but a coordinator does not expect them, queries on the affected tables fail with an IllegalStateException.
section.p: When block location loading is turned off for a filesystem, Impala handles the tables on it as if they were on an object store:

ul.li: The scheduler treats every scan range as a remote read. It no longer assigns scan ranges to the hosts that store the data, so data locality and short-circuit reads no longer help. To reduce the cost of remote reads, enable the data cache.

Scan ranges come from synthetic splits rather than from the actual blocks. Parquet files are split by the PARQUET_OBJECT_STORE_SPLIT_SIZE query option, files in other formats by the default block size of the filesystem.

Loading and refreshing large tables is much cheaper, and their file metadata takes less memory. catalogd lists the files without their block locations, using up to --max_nonhdfs_partitions_parallel_load threads per table instead of --max_hdfs_partitions_parallel_load. For Iceberg tables, the file list comes from the Iceberg metadata without accessing the files.

section.p: Because the files of Iceberg tables are not accessed during loading, Impala does not know whether they are erasure-coded. For these files, SHOW FILES shows N/A in the EC Policy column, and neither the ALLOW_ERASURE_CODED_FILES query option nor the erasure-coding counters in EXPLAIN output and query profiles apply to them. Other tables still get the erasure-coding information from the file listing.

section.title: Optional: Native Checksumming
section.p: Enabling native checksumming causes Impala to use an optimized native library for computing checksums, if that library is available.

If you installed from packages, the native checksumming library is installed and setup correctly. In such a case, no additional steps are required. Conversely, if you installed by other means, such as with tarballs, native checksumming may not be available due to missing shared objects. Finding the message "Unable to load native-hadoop library for your platform... using builtin-java classes where applicable" in the Impala logs indicates native checksumming may be unavailable. To enable native checksumming, you must build and install libhadoop.so (the
Hadoop Native Library).
